conclusion: Sampling requests draw their MTP drafts from the draft head's own truncated distribution and verify them against it (speculative sampling: accept with min(1, p/q), correct from max(0, p - q)); every emitted token still follows the target distribution. With the model's sampling preset (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) coding chat decodes 24.7% and 29.6% more tokens per second, at temperature 0.7 / top-p 0.8 8.9% and 11.0%. The speculation controller fits one latency model to every step (shared level, GPU cost per token, measured CPU expert time) and probes the choices it left; greedy drafting and acceptance are unchanged, and greedy decode is at parity to a few percent faster.

baseline.description: Frozen sixth-pass build (fngine 56c25d9) with the bench's --sample option added

selected.bench_note: The paired runs measured the tree before two later edits without runtime effect: an unreachable debug log line and the unused row-stride parameter of kernels::argmax were removed.

runtime_changes.description: The sampling kernels with a row-to-token map (draft vocabulary), a penalty overlay of the earlier drafts, a per-draw RNG subkey and no token-count increment. Greedy: penalty-adjusted argmax, one-hot. Sampling: the row's truncated distribution q is stored (DraftDistribution, 20 ids and probabilities) and the draft drawn from it.

Drafts with a stored distribution are accepted when u q(d) < p(d) and corrected from max(0, p - q) (sampling_pick_residual); other drafts keep the one-hot rule (u < p(d), correction from p without d).

The MTP bridge and the two autoregressive draft steps call sample_drafts; the bridge distribution of the accepted column and the two AR distributions stay on the device for the next step's acceptance. step() takes a flag that the drafts are the previous result's MTP drafts and checks it against them. Eager steps stage the n-gram rows before launching (they hung before).

Latency model seconds = D (1 + gamma T) + c C fitted to every step (D: fast EMA; gamma, c: normalized LMS; CPU seconds per token: EMA), acceptance averages weighted by how recently a position was offered, probe rounds one draft off the best choice within a 0.4% throughput budget.

Passes the CPU expert time of each step to the controller; the latency of the step that drew the MTP drafts is recorded after the decision about those drafts, so the decision cannot depend on the drawn values.

method: Paired processes per round (order alternating), --coding-chat -n512 -r3 --spec auto --ctx 262144, one warm-up and three measured repetitions per process, Omarchy screensaver animation paused (0.0% GPU time lost to other contexts). --sample: model preset, seed = request index. Raw reports: round7/final-*/.

greedy.note: Two earlier pairings (controller only, n = 9 each): 294.97 / 297.24 vs 295.56 / 296.96 and 298.34 / 294.68 vs 294.51 / 293.90.

offline_draft_study.note: Draft temperature x0.5-0.85, draft top-p x0.8-0.9 and argmax-when-confident hybrids were 0.1 to 4.8 points below plain sampling.

controller_replay.description: Recorded rounds of a greedy coding chat replayed through the controller with scaled CPU expert time and acceptance (tok/s)

rejected.experiment: Lookahead for the CPU expert tier (router preview from the layer input, prefetch and decode ahead)
rejected.evidence: Preview recall 67% at 44% precision; cold expert 38-48 us with 10-12 workers, blob read alone 34-45 us at 57-60 GB/s, decode + GEMM 220-260 us of one thread (gate/up decoding 71-79%). Within about 20% of the DRAM floor; estimated +5-15% for a second exchange protocol. Not built.

rejected.evidence: Hit rate 0.949 -> 0.955 in the first 512 tokens and up to 15% less CPU wait per layer, but no shorter rounds: cold start +0.6 to +8.9% (n = 5), warmed-up sampling runs -0.9 to -5.3% (n = 6). Raw reports: round7/swap1, round7/swap2.

rejected.experiment: Draft count per round from the draft head's confidence
rejected.evidence: Top probability vs acceptance correlation 0.54-0.63; cost-model gain 2.4% greedy, 0.5% sampled.

rejected.evidence: 28.4 vs 29.5 us per expert; 19% of a step's cold experts recur in the next step and one step's blobs (about 200 MB) exceed both L3s.

verification.test_speculative_real: greedy speculative output identical to plain decode on three prompts; first sampled MTP draft accepted 0.66-0.73 against its distribution vs 0.41-0.43 as a fixed token (temperature 1.5, top-k 20)
